chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم slaughtered on behalf of the Mothers of the Believers one cow each, and he himself sacrificed sixty-six camels, and 'Ali عليه السلام sacrificed thirty-four camels. He did not give the butchers anything from their coverings, nor from their garlands, nor from their hides; rather, he gave it in charity.

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْجَزَّارِينَ: the butchers who processed the slaughtered animals
key_terms.بَدَنَةً: a large sacrificial animal, especially a camel
key_terms.جُلُودِهَا: the hides or skins of the sacrificial animals
key_terms.جِلَالِهَا: the coverings or cloths placed upon the sacrificial animals
key_terms.قَلَائِدِهَا: the garlands or markers hung on the sacrificial animals

ai.seo_question: Can the hides or trappings of sacrificial animals be given to butchers as payment?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the sacrificial practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during hajj, including the number of animals sacrificed by him and by Imam 'Ali عليه السلام. It also indicates a legal ruling that the hides and related items of the sacrificial animals were not to be given as payment to butchers, but were instead to be given in charity.
